 THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT, PRAYING TO ALLOW THE APPEAL AND MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 06.04.2016 PASSED IN MVC NO.94/2015 ON THE FILE OF PRINCIPAL MACT AND PRL. DIST. AND SESSIONS JUDGE AT BIDAR BY ENHANCING THE COMPENSATION AS CLAIMED IN THE CLAIM PETITION IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING,
T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA, J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the appellants have challenged the judgment dated 06.04.2016 passed by the Principal Motor Accident Claims Tribunal and Principal District & Sessions Judge at Bidar in MVC No. 94/2015 (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal' for short).
2. The parties will be referred with respect to their status before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3. Briefly stated the facts are that, the 1st petitioner is the wife and 2nd petitioner is the minor daughter of Amit Bagbande, the deceased.

entities.text: Principal District & Sessions Judge at Bidar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The deceased, petitioners and his minor son Sai Darshan while riding motor cycle bearing registration number KA-38/K9199 near Shapur gate ring road cross at about 2-30 p.m. was hit by APSRTC bus bearing registration No.AP-29/Z-0569 from the opposite direction killing Sai Darshan on the spot and injuring the 2nd petitioner and the deceased.
The deceased died at Lalit Gayatri Hospital, Hydrabad.
Petitioners claimed compensation of Rs.99,00,000/- before the Tribunal.

They pleaded that deceased was aged 38 years, MBA graduate,
working as vice principal at Dr.Prashant Mashetty College of Business Management, Bidar drawing salary of Rs.35,000/- per month.

entities.text: Prashant Mashetty College of Business Management, Bidar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.33,28,056/- with 6% interest per annum.

Smt. Kanyakumari And Anr vs Depot Manager on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139077004/
2 4.

entities.text: Smt. Kanyakumari And Anr vs Depot Manager
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners while seeking for enhancement of compensation pleaded inadequacy in the compensation that the salary was not properly considered, that compensation towards conventional heads was not considered as per the settled principles.

5. Heard the arguments of Sri.Sheshadri Jaishankar for Sri. Amareshwar S Rawoor, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri. Gangashetty Patil, learned counsel for the 1st respondent/APSRTC.
6.

According to the learned counsel for petitioners, the deceased was a MBA postgraduate, was working as Lecturer, because of his merit was appointed as Vice Principal with higher salary of Rs.35,000/- per month, that compensation under conventional heads has been settled and accordingly, he sought for re-assessment and enhancement.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for the 1st respondent/APSRTC contended that the Tribunal has rightly considered the income at Rs.29,063/-, there is no proof of income of Rs.35,000/-, that the college which appointed the deceased is a private institution not Government or Government aided Institution, that much of salary will not be paid.
It is also submitted that, compensation under conventional heads were already settled and he has no objection for assessment accordingly and supported the impugned judgment.
8. We have given our anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the parties and perused the records.
9. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident, death of the deceased and the petitioners being the wife and minor daughter, as dependents are entitled to claim compensation.
As indicated by Ex.P.19 & 20 the salary certificate and Form No.16, the deceased was served as Lecturer in Business Management, at Bheemanna Khandre Institute of Technology, Bhalki.

entities.text: Bheemanna Khandre Institute of Technology, Bhalki
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Ex.P21 indicate that the deceased was appointed as Vice Principal of Dr.Prashant Mashetty College of Business Management, Bidar on a consolidated salary of Rs.35,000/- on 25-07-2014.

entities.text: Prashant Mashetty College of Business Management, Bidar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: So it is clear that the deceased was a salaried person.
The Tribunal considered the income at Rs.29,063/- as net salary as lecturer, decline to accept the new appointment of the deceased for the reason that it was just one month prior to the accident.

On the date of accident deceased was not serving at Bheemanna Khandre Institute of Technology, Bhalki, hence it is not proper to hold him for his lesser income post when he gained the higher income post.

entities.text: Bheemanna Khandre Institute of Technology, Bhalki
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Hence, we are of the view that the income assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.29,063/- is on the lower side and we assess it at Rs.35,000/- per month.
10. As seen from the impugned judgment, the Tribunal has assessed Rs.20,000/- each towards consortium, Rs.20,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses.
The tribunal has not considered future prospects for no reasons; hence it is required to be considered while assessing the loss of dependency.

11. By applying the principles laid down in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others -2017 ACJ 680, 30% is the future prospects required to be added while assessing the income of the deceased, PM reports indicate the age of the deceased at 42.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others -2017 ACJ 680, 30%
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
While assessing the compensation under conventional heads, the Tribunal has ignored the settled principles, which Smt. Kanyakumari And Anr vs Depot Manager on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139077004/
3 require modification.

entities.text: Kanyakumari And Anr vs Depot Manager on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation - (2009)6 SCC 121, the applicable multiplier for the age of '42' is '14' and it was correctly applied by the Tribunal.
12.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation - (2009)6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
If all these factors are taken into consideration, the assessment of loss of dependency would be:
Income of the deceased Rs.35,000/-, out of it IT TDS of 10% and PT of Rs.200/- is excluded, it comes to Rs.35,000/- - Rs.3,700/- = Rs.31.300/-, if Rs.9,390/- (30% Future Prospects) is added, it comes to Rs.40,690/- per annum.

The petitioners are the wife and minor daughter, they are 2 in number, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased i.e., Rs.40,690/- -
Rs.13,563/- = Rs.27,127/-.
The compensation towards loss of dependency works out at Rs.27,127/-x12=Rs.3,25,524/- multiplied by '14' comes to Rs.45,55,336/-.

13. Under the conventional heads, Rs.40,000/- towards consortium to wife, Rs.40,000/- to minor daughter towards love and affection, towards loss of estate and funeral expenses Rs.15,000/- each is assessed.
Then total compensation comes to Rs.46,67,336/- as against Rs.33,25,056/- awarded by the Tribunal.
In our opinion, it is the just compensation to which the petitioners are entitled in the facts and circumstances of the case.
Thereby the petitioners are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.13,42,280/- rounded off to Rs.13,42,000/-.
Accordingly, the appeal deserves to be allowed.

14. In the result, the following:
ORDER
The appeal is allowed in part.
The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.

The petitioners are entitled to total  compensation of Rs.46,67,336/- as against  Rs.33,25,056/- granted by the Tribunal, an enhanced compensation of Rs.13,42,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.
Rest of the judgment and award of the Tribunal is kept intact.
Office is directed to transfer the amount if any in deposit, to the Tribunal, forthwith.
